cli: reject --port values outside 0-65535

## 📝 Summary

Closes #11521

`--port` was declared with `type=int`, so Click accepted values outside the valid TCP port range and the server later failed with `OverflowError: bind(): port must be 0-65535`.

This changes the user-facing `--port` options (`edit`, `run`, `new`, `tutorial`, and `development preview`) to `click.IntRange(0, 65535)` so out-of-range values fail immediately with exit code 2 and a Click usage error. Internal LSP/pylsp `--port` options are left untouched since they are not user input.

Added unit tests in `tests/_cli/test_cli.py` covering out-of-range `--port` values across all five commands.

## 👋 First time contributor introduction

I am Tejas, a software developer who uses marimo for interactive Python notebooks and tooling experiments. Looking forward to contributing fixes to the CLI and developer experience.

## 📋 Pre-Review Checklist

- [ ] For large changes, or changes that affect the public API: this change was discussed or approved through an issue, on [Discord](https://marimo.io/discord?ref=pr), or the community [discussions](https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo/discussions) (Please provide a link if applicable).
- [x] Any AI generated code has been reviewed line-by-line by the human PR author, who stands by it.
- [ ] Video or media evidence is provided for any visual changes.

## ✅ Merge Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/marimo-team/marimo/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Documentation has been updated where applicable, including docstrings for API changes.
- [x] Tests have been added for the changes made.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(markdown): stop remounting canvases on every streamed token

### Ship change · `ship-change · local · claude-code`

Refs #512 (follow-up: the flicker came back while a reply streams).

`Markdown` passed its `pre`, `a` and `blockquote` renderers to `react-markdown` as inline functions. Each render therefore gave React a new component type, and it remounted those subtrees. While a reply streams, `Markdown` re-renders on every token, so every canvas in the conversation was rebuilt: its iframe reloaded at the default 420 px and then grew back, which showed as flicker on each turn. Mermaid diagrams were redrawn on every token for the same reason.

**Change.** Those three renderers don't read the component's props, so they move to a module constant, `STABLE_COMPONENTS`; only `li` (which depends on `onTaskChange`) stays per render. No behaviour change besides the remounts.

**Not covered.** When the streamed reply is replaced by the saved message at the end of a turn, a canvas inside that reply still reloads once.

**Checks.** Frontend typecheck, oxlint, the 170 frontend unit tests and the quality ratchet passed on the original commit; not yet tried in a running instance.

**Docs.** No doc change (bug fix); changelog fragment `changelog.d/markdown-stable-renderers.fixed.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

fix(router): never report a dynamic route as hidden by the API reference

Closes #619

With `src/routes/[lang]/index.tsx`, `nexy dev` printed at start that the route "is never served at /docs" and "at /openapi.json", and told the developer to move the API reference or rename the route. The route is served at `/fr`, `/en` and every other value: it only matched `/docs` because its parameter accepts any segment.

`reserved_paths._claims` now first checks that the literal part of the route, before its first parameter, is the reserved path (`_literally_at`). So:

| Route | Reported at `/docs` |
|---|---|
| `/docs` | yes (unchanged) |
| `/docs/{slug:path}` | yes (unchanged: `/docs` redirects to `/docs/`, which it answers) |
| `/docs/intro` | no (unchanged) |
| `/{lang}` | no (was yes) |
| `/{path:path}` | no (was yes) |

The same holds at `/openapi.json`.

## Tests

`tests/unit/nexy/routers/test_reserved_paths.py`: a dynamic first segment and a root catch-all are not reported; the existing cases above still are. `python scripts/verify.py` passes (every gate, diff coverage included).

benchmarks.task_description:
Fix device stuck offline after re-pairing

Zigbee2MQTT publishes a re-paired or renamed device's availability before its new `bridge/devices` list. The tracker dropped that message because the name wasn't in its list yet, so the device kept its old offline state while live messages kept arriving.

- Availability for a name not in the device list yet is kept (latest per name, capped at 200 per network, memory only) and applied when the next list arrives.
- A device coming back into the list starts with unknown availability and its open outage is closed, instead of carrying its old offline state.

Tested: ruff clean, 1377 tests pass (5 new in `tests/test_repair_availability.py`). On the test HA with the simulated network: device marked offline, dropped from the list, sent online, then list republished. It ends active and online with the outage closed.

Closes #73

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(harness-ui): fade chat text across its full width on narrow screens

## Summary

On a phone, chat text that scrolled under the faded area above the composer stayed sharp in a strip at the left edge, while the rest of the line faded and blurred. The same happened in a thinner strip at the right edge and under the header fade. The sharp fragments looked like broken content sitting on top of the fade.

In narrow chat layouts (reader at 600px or less) the transcript runs from the reader's start edge to its scrollbar. The header and composer fades still used the fixed 12px desktop insets, so they stopped 12px short of the text on both sides. This predates the recent phone work; it is most visible on phones because the text column there touches the reader edges.

The fades now cover the same width as the text column. They stop only at a classic scrollbar, whose width the fades measure from the reader (overlay scrollbars on phones measure zero), so a desktop scrollbar stays crisp. Wide layouts keep their existing insets, and the Work log reader is unchanged.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: the formula line under the composer fade stays sharp at the left and right edges](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/263c8cd0-8185-4fcd-97f9-cfd1742391d6) | ![After: the formula line fades evenly across its full width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ceb4a8e-2755-459b-a408-61117ca64336) |

This aligns the implementation with the [WebUI design guidelines](spec/a13n-harness-ui/webui/06-design-guidelines.md): content fades continuously toward the header and composer, with no hard seam across a readable line.

## Related issue

Reported from the mobile Harness WebUI after #1779; no linked issue.

## Validation

In Chrome at 390×844 with phone emulation, the fades now span exactly the reader's text column (12–372px beside a 6px classic scrollbar, 12–378px with emulated overlay scrollbars). A 520px desktop window keeps its scrollbar outside the fade, and a 1280px window keeps the 12px insets. A new test covers the scrollbar measurement for classic and overlay scrollbars and the default insets without a reader. The existing conversation, transcript continuity, opening and Work log tests pass, and the WebUI typechecks.

Gap: not tested on a physical iOS or Android device.

## Checklist
